method: per laser maximum: median brightness and dark fraction of the 0.32 m orthophoto inside the crown radius (floor 1.5 m) about the apex; open = median >= 88 and dark < 10% (the clear-fell calibration of trace-canopy-changes.mjs), crown = median <= 80 and dark >= 15%; distinct = the 1.4-2.4 radius annulus reads 25 brighter than the disc; a promotion also needs excess green >= 3
limitations: A May capture: birch and aspen are half in leaf, so a thin deciduous crown on turf can read unclear; unclear is kept, never promoted.
The imagery confirms a crown stood there in 2026; heights and radii stay the laser's 2021 measurement.
A crown inside closed forest cannot be distinguished from its neighbours in either record; it stays in the stand field.

census.question: trees the leaf-off 2021 laser has no maximum for, visible only in the 2026 imagery
census.method: dark (brightness <= 80), green (excess green >= 3) 4-connected components of the 0.32 m orthophoto inside 90 m of the hole lines, outside every laser crown (its radius + 1.5 m) and the shadow capsule each crown casts at the capture's solar bearing (45.06 deg, 1.3 x height), outside buildings (6 m) and water (3 m); components of 3-150 m2 with bounding-box compactness >= 0.35
census.verdict: NOT ADOPTED. Drawn over the imagery, the hits sit in the gaps between shadow capsules inside closed forest and in dark rough beside greens; the rule finds shade, not stems. A tree the laser never measured needs a detector that reads the crown AND its own shadow on open turf, and a height from that shadow against the solar position, which this pass does not attempt. Recorded so the same rule is not tried again.
